steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a cookie sheet.

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter, brown sugar and white sugar until smooth. Beat in the egg and vanilla. Sift together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and espresso powder; stir into the creamed mixture. Finally, stir in the chocolate chips.
Drop dough by heaping tablespoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheet. Cookies should be 1 1/2 to 2 inches apart. You should have 12 to 15 large cookies.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven. For crispier cookies, bake 2 minutes longer. Remove from baking sheets to cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Neiman Marcus Chocolate Chip Cookie
raw_recipe.description: This is the famous Neiman Marcus Chocolate Chip Cookie Recipe. There has been a myth that someone was charged $250 for the recipe, but that was never true. This is now their official cookie recipe, and it’s free to everyone.
raw_recipe.name: Neiman Marcus Chocolate Chip Cookie

review.reviewBody: I recently made this recipe after printing it out from the Neiman Marcus website, and it says to bake the cookies in a 300 degree oven for about 20 minutes (not at 375 degrees for 8 to 10 minutes). These cookies stayed very moist and chewy much longer than any other chocolate chip cookies I've made, and I think the reason is that they were baked at a lower temperature.

This is completely different from the one that I received back when I first went on the net in 1999. 

2 cups butter 
4 cups flour 
2 tsp. baking soda 
2 cups granulated sugar 
2 cups brown sugar 
5 cups blended oatmeal (measure oatmeal and blend in blender to a fine powder) 
24 oz. chocolate chips 
1 tsp. salt 
1 8 oz. Hershey bar (grated) 
4 eggs 
2 tsp. baking powder 
3 cups chopped nuts (your choice) 
2 tsp. vanilla 
Cream the butter and both sugars. Add eggs and vanilla; mix together with flour, oatmeal, salt, baking powder, and soda. Add chocolate chips, Hershey bar and nuts. Roll into balls and place two inches apart on a cookie sheet..Bake for 10 minutes at 375 degrees. Makes 112 cookies.. Have Fun!!!

This is the original recipe that I got back then with the hoax that it was a Neiman Marcus recipe. Either I have made this recipe above a million times and everyone who tries it loves it. It's a huge recipe but it can be halved.

Great cookie! I made them a lot smaller than suggested at just one tablespoon per cookie using a small ice cream scoop and got 6 dozen cookies. Great taste with the instant espresso power, and I flatened the cookie with a Fork dipped in more of the instant espresso to give them a slightly different look. As suggested by another reviewer, I substituted 3/4 of a cup of the flour with a cup of rolled oats that I chopped to a fine powder in a food processor, just to give the cookies a but more substance.

I love this cookies. I tweaked the recipe a little bit such as lower the white sugar to 2 tbs, 50% walnuts 50% chocolate chips, lower the temperature to 300 F, lower the cooking time to 20 minutes. The result was amazing, thick, soft and nutty.. just the way we like it ! Next time I will add a little bit more of espresso.

I've seen a few variations of the recipe on the internet. I remember reading about this hoax when it first came out in the mid-1990's. The first one I read, it used oatmeal, which didn't turn out so great. This one doesn't use oatmeal, and it turned out so much better. To make it better yet, I added a little bit of vanilla pudding mix (the instant kind) to add softness and prevented the cookies from getting stale so quick. I aslo adjusted the oven temperature, to 350 instead of 375 degrees.

I've made the original for 20 years, they do call for grounded oats and shaved chocolate. I use dark brown sugar, and I make my dough the day before baking. Letting them rest in the refrigerator for 24 hours really marries the flavored.

This is not the Neiman Marcus cookie. It’s good, but definitely not close to the store one. Flavor is good, the dough was very dense before baking with food consistency. We only did 1 cup of chocolate chips because we thought the extra half cup would be too much. 

We baked two batches. One at 375° for about 10 minutes, and they were raw in the middle. So we baked them for an extra 5 min at 375°. The other batch we did at 300° For 20 minutes and they were perfect. These spread out more. 

I will continue looking for the true neiman Marcus cookie.
I have an old original copy of this recipe that was received back in the early 80s that calls for ground oats & shaved chocolate. It can be halved or even quartered which makes about 28 cookies.
I love this recipe and cooked it at 300 for 20 minutes. Neiman or not loved it. I did cut out the 1/2 extra chocolate chips for some toasted hazelnuts and coconut. Loved them! Definitely a keeper!
Delicious flavor and the ground oats make a light cookie. They don't spread much, so I press the spoonfuls down a tiny bit.

The change I made was I added 1 1/2 tsp of reg. coffee (community coffee, dark roast) and baked the cookies at 300 degrees for twenty mins. But I remember when I first acquired this recipe there was oats in it that were pulverized in a blender but whatever, awesome cookies.
nope. perfection doesn't need changes
Not even close to the original.
This is NOT the recipe that went viral in the 90s. (I should know, I was there, and I got the email.) This recipe is BORING and barely different from a standard chocolate chip cookie.

I think i made mine a little thicker, they ended up being under baked in the middle... I cooked them for about 5 more minutes and they were still way chewier than I liked but tbh the flavor of them was fantastic past the texture difference, ill be making these again one day and correcting my beginner mistakes :)
Leave out the coffee- it does not help! And how is this really different from the time honored variations of the original Toll House Cookie! That's still the best!
Delicious
The “original” contained oats and shaved Hershey bars. This IS NOT the original recipe.
It fits the bill for over indulgence but worth it when you want to reward and treat yourself or your guests.

I know for a fact that the story of the woman who loved the cookie so much had asked if she could have the recipe is VERY TRUE. She was never told how much and only found out she was charged $250 on her credit card for it. It was before 1992, since the man who told us about it worked with the woman at IBM in Ontario Canada, and was also my mothers boyfriend at the time. My mom passed away in 1992. We got a big kick out of the story. She was so ticked off about the charge of the recipe that she shared the recipe with everyone who wanted it. What is missing from your recipe is the ground up oatmeal. But they are fantastic cookies.
